note: General writing rules for a claims review demo. They are not legal advice and not a compliance standard.

rules.text: Don't say a product is certified, compliant or approved without naming who said so.
Don't call anything unbreakable, tamper-proof or 100% secure.
Don't say "patented" unless a patent has actually issued.
Every number needs a stated source and date.
Words like "every", "all" and "never" need proof that they're true in every case.
Don't promise a legal result, such as "admissible in court."
Say plainly what the product doesn't do, next to what it does.
Don't name a customer or partner without permission.
Don't describe a planned feature as if it exists today. Label it as planned.
Don't use "guaranteed" unless a written guarantee exists.
Don't claim to be "the first", "the only" or "the leading" without proof.
Don't compare against a competitor without a current, checkable source.
Don't quote a person or company without their approval and the exact wording.
Don't state a result as typical if it came from one test or one customer.
Don't imply that a regulator, government or standards body endorses the product unless it has said so in writing.
